title: Solos, vamping and band cues
summary: How Palmer varies a solo, vamps, and how bands know who takes breaks; ends with the first Chicago place on Wells.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: When you play a solo, what do you try to do?

Well, sometimes I take a solo and when they're playing, they're vamping me, see? And I'm playing this solo. I may take it up in 16ths, see? I may take it up in 16ths, play a whole note and use some 16ths with it. But I'm going to use 16ths in the place of it, but with the same melody, see? Just like you say. I may go. See, I'm going on with the melody right on, but I'm putting something in between there, see? See? See, I get on back on that part. I never stay in that part. See, I go away from it, see. Because if you continue playing with him, with his melody, you know, I keep playing the melody, well, that takes the sweetness away from the beauty, away from the peace from him. See, he might have a nice part to play, see. Well, I'll start him off with it, see. Every boy to get in together, I start him right off with it, like, I'm going to stay with him, and after a while, I'm gone. They got a lot of little tricks in it, see, playing that way. And it helps the other fella, and a lot of fellas likes to take down, you know, when they're playing the melody and like that. Because all you got to do is just bow his head. If he's going to take down, he's losing the lead or something. Look over there at me, I'll hold him eight measures and play it for him, and then I'll turn him loose and go right on back into that part. Vamping on trombone is the best thing that a man could do. Vamping on trombone and playing an off melody. That sweetens the band right up, see. Playing if you're playing. Not all the way through, boom, boom, boom. You know, you heard them records some further. He couldn't go nowhere but vamp, vamp, vamp, vamp. And that's all he could do. By vamping, you mean just by. That's just vamping, you see, like that nine, and you play it, and then get away from it, see. You vamp it, get away from it, take some lead, see. And you're listening. That's when you're playing a piece, and you're playing it by music or by ear. Listen for the guy, what he's doing over there, see. Whatever he's doing over there, you do it different but do it in units, see, together. They say, that's a sweet band, sure. It's going to be sweet when they're all working together. And the guys used to point out to fellas, you know, who they want. Take the break. Take the break. Fellas stood up one night, about two hours, said, how do you fellas know when or who's going to take it? He don't know. See, even the leader just pointing over to the fella, you know. He don't know.
